stories.title: argenx reports positive Phase 2 FB102 results in celiac disease
stories.takeaway: CD122 blockade improved villus architecture during gluten challenge.
stories.what_happened: A 126-person randomized Phase 2 study met its villus-height-to-crypt-depth primary endpoint (p=0.0176); argenx plans Phase 3.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows a clinically useful epithelial structural endpoint linking immunology to intestinal injury models.
stories.caveat: Only topline company results are available; durability and long-term safety are unknown.

stories.title: Biohub and partners back a $1.8B push for predictive cell biology
stories.takeaway: Large-scale perturbation datasets are becoming strategic AI infrastructure.
stories.what_happened: Biohub announced a $1.8B initiative combining its own funds, private investment, DOE support and NIH-coordinated datasets.
stories.why_it_matters: Standardized single-cell perturbation data could complement controlled host–microbiome and mechanical exposures on chips.
stories.caveat: The total includes existing federal investments; industry funders get temporary preferential data access.

stories.title: NIH's $7.1M QuSAFE challenge targets live sensing in NAMs
stories.takeaway: NIH is prioritizing non-destructive, longitudinal readouts inside organ chips.
stories.what_happened: The NCATS quantum-enabled sensing competition opens registration October 25 and offers $7.1M in prizes.
stories.why_it_matters: Scalable redox and barrier monitoring could strengthen multiplex gut-chip research and funding opportunities.
stories.caveat: A genuine quantum-enabled sensing modality is mandatory; ordinary TEER instrumentation alone is out of scope.

stories.title: Biotech IPOs rebound to 23 in 2026's first nine months
stories.takeaway: Biotech capital markets are reopening after a long drought.
stories.what_happened: Twenty-three biotech IPOs occurred through September, versus eight during all of 2025, according to William Blair data reported October 8.
stories.why_it_matters: Potentially favorable for translational-biotech financing and career mobility.
stories.caveat: IPO counts do not prove durable hiring, cash runway or drug-development success.

stories.title: Microbiota-supportive diet associates with lower IBD risk, not clearly Crohn's
stories.takeaway: A large cohort finds a 16% lower IBD incidence, driven mainly by ulcerative colitis.
stories.what_happened: A September 3 peer-reviewed study, newly highlighted October 8, followed 208,143 participants; none of nine candidate protein mediators survived multiple-testing correction.
stories.why_it_matters: Supports testing diet-derived substrates as controlled microbiome exposures while distinguishing UC from Crohn's responses.
stories.caveat: Observational associations are not causal; no significant Crohn's-specific association was established.
